text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
OSLOBODJENJE

- Bosnian company "Energoinvest" is due to meet Russian gas supplier to discuss issues related to gas delivery to Bosnia in Pale on Thursday, official from a High Representative office in Sarajevo said.
- An OSCE vehicle was hijacked by masked gunmen on the road from Pale to Sarajevo and taken to Pale, an OSCE spokesman said.
- Bosnia's collective cabinet failed again on Wednesday to adopt foreign trade law. Disputed issue refers to "special ties between Bosnia's entities and neighbouring country".

- Bosnia's federation Prime Minister Edhem Bicakcic and International Monetary Fund (IMF) head of mission in Bosnia, Scott Brown, discussed in Sarajevo further measures required for Brussels donor conference set for mid-April.

- Chairman of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, Danish Foreign Affairs minister Niels Helveg Petersen, and Croat member in Bosnia's collective presidency Kresimir Zubak discuss preparations and conditions for the upcoming local polls scheduled for September.
- The first Turkish bank opened its branch in Sarajevo on Wednesday.
- Bosnian Moslems who used to work in aluminium company currently in the Croat-held Mostar still cannot even think of returning to work, Rusmir Cisic, member of Mostar city council says.
- Swedish government and a geodesic company donated 1.5 million German Marks to geodesic sector in Bosnia, head of Bosnian department says.
- Room with a view on Adriatic sea will cost 20 German Marks per day this year, it was said at an international tourist fair in Sarajevo on Wednesday.
- Experts say that Bosnia will need 20 to 30 years to be completely cleared from mines dispersed throughout Bosnia during its 1992-95 war.
- Turkish and Italian milk companies provided 3.5 million German Marks for restoring production in the north of Bosnia.
- Vienna authorities donated three firetrucks to Sarajevo fire brigade, governor of the Sarajevo canton says.
DNEVNI AVAZ
- Moslem chairman of Bosnia's three-man presidency Alija Izetbegovic and international top official in Bosnia Carl Bildt discuss the implementation of the Dayton peace agreement.
- Federation's budget draft law is due to be adopted on Thursday by federation government.
- Sir Martin Garrod, head of High Representative's Mostar office says in an interview that joint police forces in the divided town of Mostar will most probably be formed before April 15.
- Sarajevo police discover cache of explosive devices at a Sarajevo cemetry, interior ministry reports.
- Federation Prime Minister Edhem Bicakcic renewes contacts with an international oil company "Amoco" which will check if Bosnia is rich with oil. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864.
